messages:
customer-jane: Hey team — since this morning our inference calls are 503ing and we see ~200-300ms extra RTT. We deploy to eu-west1 but traffic looks like it's hitting us-west1. Any idea?

sarah-support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a failed request_id and one curl repro? Also did you change any VPC peering or proxy config recently? :thinking:

customer-jane: request_id=req_2026-03-17_09:42:11_67b9
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
We didn't touch peering, but the on-prem edge team pushed a firewall update last night.

alex-eng-infra: Thanks. Two quick asks: 1) can you share the X-Redwood-Request, X-Region headers from the failing response? 2) paste a traceroute (mtr/traceroute) to api.redwood.ai from your onprem box.

customer-jane: headers from a failing response:
```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
X-Redwood-Request: req_2026-03-17_09:42:11_67b9
X-Region-Used: us-west1
X-Cache: MISS
```
traceroute output:
```
traceroute to api.redwood.ai (34.120.88.7), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  1.0 ms  1.0 ms  1.1 ms
 2  198.51.100.2  14.3 ms  13.9 ms  14.0 ms
 3  203.0.113.7  145.2 ms  146.0 ms  145.8 ms
 4  34.120.88.7  146.5 ms  146.7 ms  146.6 ms
```

alex-eng-infra: Hmm region header shows us-west1. That suggests your egress path is hairpinning into our us-west POP. Could be SNAT at your peering NAT or proxy rewriting source IP so smart-routing picks us-west. Can you run `curl -v` and include `--resolve api.redwood.ai:<port>:<eu-pop-ip>` to force eu, just to verify eu endpoint works?

customer-jane: Forcing EU endpoint returns 200 and normal latency. So service in eu is fine.

mike-oncall: Noted. I'm seeing a spike in cross-region egress for that account starting 09:30 UTC — routing decision matches us-west due to source IP mapping. Likely onprem NAT collapsed private IPs to a public IP we classify as US.

ops-ryan: Can you share a sample conntrack / SNAT mapping or the public IP you're SNATting to? We'll check our geo table.

customer-jane: public egress IP is 52.12.34.56 (we rotate via their firewall).

alex-eng-infra: That IP is geolocated to US-West in our IP->region mapping. If your SNAT gateway is in EU but advertises a US egress, our smart routing will prefer us-west. Two remediation options: 1) update your NAT/peering to preserve original EU source IP (no hairpin SNAT), or 2) ask us to pin your traffic to eu-west1 for that account until you fix NAT. Which do you prefer?

customer-jane: We need a quick pin because the billing spike is worrying — we've seen egress charges for cross-region traffic.

billing-ella: I see an unexplained egress charge starting at 09:30 UTC on account acme-corp. If pinned to eu, we can retroactively flag for review but need support engineer confirmation.

sarah-support: I'll escalate. @alex-eng-infra can you open a temporary region-lock for acme-corp and add a routing exception for src IP 52.12.34.56? Also can you add a short TTL on the geo mapping so rotated IPs update quicker?

alex-eng-infra: Starting to create a routing exception — will route requests with X-Customer-ID: acme-corp OR source=52.12.34.56 to eu-west1. Deploying a canary change now.

deploy-bot: deploy started: route-exception-acme-2141594820 by alex-eng-infra — canary 5%

mike-oncall: Canary looks healthy. 5% to eu-west shows 200s and normal latency. Increasing to 100%.

deploy-bot: deploy complete: route-exception-acme-2141594820 — 100%

customer-jane: Confirmed — requests now land in eu-west and 503s stopped. Latency back to normal. Thank you. :tada:

alex-eng-infra: We'll keep the exception for 48 hours while you fix NAT. Please push a config to preserve source IP or use an EU egress IP range. Also we'll add a note to our docs about rotating SNAT gateways and geo mapping.

billing-ella: I'll hold a billing review and credit any obvious cross-region charges during the incident window.

ops-ryan: FYI, I'll add a monitoring alert to detect sudden source-IP geolocation shifts for accounts with pinned regions.

customer-jane: Appreciate the quick help. We'll follow up when firewall team has a permanent fix.

sarah-support: Closing loop here once acme confirms NAT fix. Thanks everyone :)
